metaData.originalTitle: Making sense of conflicting labour market signals
metaData.title: Making sense of conflicting labour market signals
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: This paper introduces a novel framework that extracts four interpretable 'narrative factors' from 94 US labour market indicators to resolve conflicting signals, revealing that the post-pandemic soft landing was driven by both cooling demand and an unusual decline in short-run labour supply.
metaData.summary: This VoxEU column addresses the challenge of interpreting conflicting US labour market signals—where payroll growth slows, vacancies decline, but unemployment remains low and wage growth persists. The authors propose a framework that uses principal components analysis on 94 monthly and quarterly time series (1960–2026) and rotates them with sign restrictions from textbook models to produce four 'narrative factors': labour demand, long-run labour supply, short-run labour supply, and matching efficiency. The framework formalizes the narratives policymakers already use implicitly. A key finding is that the post-pandemic soft landing was not solely a demand-side story; a simultaneous contraction in short-run labour supply suppressed the unemployment rate by about 0.75 percentage points and reduced monthly payroll growth by roughly 90,000 jobs. This explains the paradox of households finding it harder to get jobs while firms struggle to fill vacancies. The column emphasizes that no single indicator should be interpreted in isolation and provides a systematic method for organizing noisy, real-time data into coherent economic narratives.

mainPoints.point: Conflicting labour market signals can be resolved by extracting a small set of interpretable 'narrative factors' from a large dataset.
mainPoints.explanation: The framework uses 94 indicators and sign restrictions to identify four factors—labour demand, long-run supply, short-run supply, and matching efficiency—that jointly explain cyclical dynamics.

mainPoints.point: The post-pandemic soft landing was driven by both cooling demand and a simultaneous decline in short-run labour supply.
mainPoints.explanation: This joint contraction suppressed the unemployment rate and reduced payroll growth, explaining why the labour market did not deteriorate as much as demand alone would suggest.

mainPoints.point: Short-run labour supply, not just labour demand, is a critical cyclical driver often overlooked in policy debates.
mainPoints.explanation: It captures the effective elasticity of labour supply—how easily firms can hire without raising wages—and is strongly countercyclical, tightening late in expansions.

mainPoints.point: No single labour market indicator should be interpreted in isolation; the cross-sectional richness of data disciplines the narrative.
mainPoints.explanation: The framework naturally handles data revisions, missing observations, and publication lags, providing a more robust real-time assessment than relying on a few headline numbers.

keyQuotes: Instead of asking, 'What does the unemployment rate say?', we ask: 'What combination of labour demand, labour supply, and matching frictions can jointly explain the full set of labour market data?'

The weakness in short-run labour supply reduced nonfarm payroll growth by roughly 90,000 jobs per month over the past year while simultaneously suppressing the unemployment rate by approximately 0.75 percentage points.

A decline in vacancies need not imply collapsing labour demand but can reflect declining turnover. A lower payroll growth rate need not signal labour market deterioration if short-run labour supply is weakening at the same time.

relatedArticles.title: Economic Mechanisms Against AGI Unemployment
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Details key economic principles—the Baumol effect, comparative advantage, and new industry creation—that explain why technological progress consistently creates jobs.

relatedArticles.title: Why some digital payment systems replace cash and others don’t
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This column argues that instant digital payment systems can replace cash only when adoption quickly reaches low-income users, requiring low costs, dense networks, supply-side coordination, awareness, and trust.

relatedArticles.title: Fighting misinformation with truth: Why mainstream news matters on social media
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: An experiment on X during the 2024 US presidential campaign shows that nudging users to think before sharing outperforms fact-checking in reducing misinformation, and that exposure to uncontroversial true news is key.

relatedArticles.title: Speech by Governor Barr on supervision and regulation
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Fed Governor Barr warns that the current wave of deregulation in banking, including lower capital and liquidity requirements and weaker supervision, is increasing financial stability risks and will likely lead to severe long-term economic costs that outweigh any short-term benefits.
